Your wallet. Your data.

How information moves through the live FloatSheets beta.

Updated 24 September 2026 · Live beta

{01}

Wallet and trading information.

FloatSheets uses your connected public wallet address to show balances, positions, vault shares, and transaction history. Quote and transaction requests send the information needed for the action, such as your address, market, direction, and amount, through the frontend service to the API. Wallet signatures authorize actions; FloatSheets does not ask you to enter a private key or recovery phrase.

{02}

Public blockchain records.

Submitted transactions, addresses, transfers, and contract events are public on Robinhood Chain. Others can inspect and link this activity to a wallet. Disconnecting, clearing browser storage, or asking FloatSheets to remove data cannot erase confirmed blockchain records.

{03}

Information stored in your browser.

The dashboard saves preferences such as theme, reduced motion, sidebar state, and notification settings in browser storage. Recent-activity entries are also stored locally. Wallet software may retain connection sessions. Display-name and newsletter preferences, where entered, are device-local. Actual token balances and positions are read from the chain, not created by local storage.

{04}

Service and infrastructure data.

The API stores market configuration, price observations, and quote samples in PostgreSQL to support market displays and risk checks. If you enable liquidation email alerts, it stores your wallet address and email address, plus verification and delivery state. If you link Telegram alerts, it stores your wallet address, Telegram chat identifier and username, link state, and delivery state. You can disable either channel in dashboard settings; email details can also be removed there. Contact us to request removal of a Telegram link. Application request logs include the method, request path, response status, duration, and request ID. Hosting, RPC, and wallet-connection providers may also process technical information such as IP addresses and connection metadata when handling requests.

{05}

Other service providers.

The frontend is hosted on Vercel and the backend on Render. Wallet connections use RainbowKit and wallet connectors, including WalletConnect where selected; chain reads use RPC services. Resend processes alert email addresses and delivers verification and liquidation messages. These providers and your wallet have their own privacy practices. Following social or explorer links takes you to external services.

{06}

Your controls.

Use dashboard settings to disable email or Telegram liquidation alerts, clear the email address, and manage linked Telegram alerts. Contact us to request removal of stored Telegram link data. Disconnect your wallet to end the active connection, manage connected sites in your wallet, and clear this site’s browser storage to remove device-local preferences and activity. Clearing local history does not delete on-chain records or service-provider logs. Do not put confidential information in public transactions or optional text fields.

{07}

Contact.

FloatSheets is the service name. Send privacy questions or requests to security@floatsheets.app, without including private keys or recovery phrases. Requests concerning third-party services may also need to be directed to the relevant provider.
